clause (the spec's words): Pinned app tile: "with 'Dentist' inside the feed's 24 hours"
why it cannot hold as written: The row's own Dentist is at 14:00 TODAY and is deleted from the app two clauses earlier ("delete from the app → the provider row is gone"); run after 15:00 it would also be outside the feed's window (now … now + 24 h) even if it were kept.
what the driver asserts instead: e4.sh leg E driver-inserts a second "Dentist" into Tessera starting 2 h from the device's now (1 h long) and runs the pinned-tile comparison with that one; it is deleted in the restore.

clause (the spec's words): Pinned app tile: "the pinned tile's dump holds the same face text as the CALENDAR slot tile"
why it cannot hold as written: Pin to Start gives a MEDIUM tile and the baseline's CALENDAR slot tile is WIDE; phase 01's tile rule draws a calendar event's lines on a WIDE tile only (start/TileView.kt:459, `face.eventLines.isNotEmpty() && model.size == TileSize.WIDE`), so at the pinned size the two dumps differ whatever CalendarFeed publishes (run 1 kept: E4-run1-pinned-tile-compared-at-different-sizes — slot "Calendar|Dentist|6:05 PM", pinned "Calendar|Thursday|1" only).
what the driver asserts instead: At the pinned size (MEDIUM) e4.sh asserts the pinned tile shows CalendarFeed's day face (day name + number: content only its component key can give it) and RECORDs both tiles' texts; then it sets the pinned tile to the slot tile's size in the layout file (layout_restore, verified) and asserts both tiles show Dentist's face and the SAME set of face texts over 16 dumps, plus the two `[engine] publish` lines (feed:calendar and cmp:…CalendarActivity, faces=2). Whether a MEDIUM pinned Calendar tile should show event text is the owner's call (phase 01's rule today says no).

clause (the spec's words): The write guard's JVM test … runs and passes, its output in the row's log
why it cannot hold as written: A row writer never runs ./gradlew (the lead builds), so the driver cannot run the test itself.
what the driver asserts instead: e22.sh leg J reads the lead's result file app/build/test-results/testDebugUnitTest/TEST-app.tileshell.calendar.CalendarWriteGuardTest.xml: asserts 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped, that the file is newer than the test's source and CalendarWriteGuard.kt, copies every test case's verdict into the row's log, and asserts one named passing case for each allowed case and each refusal the row lists (14 assertions).

clause (the spec's words): The guard's JVM test (the People write guard line, (5)) runs and passes, its output in the row's log
why it cannot hold as written: A row writer never runs ./gradlew (the lead builds), so the driver cannot run the test itself.
what the driver asserts instead: e28.sh reads the lead's result file app/build/test-results/testDebugUnitTest/TEST-app.tileshell.people.PeopleWriteGuardTest.xml: tests > 0, failures = 0, errors = 0, skipped = 0, the file newer than PeopleWriteGuard.kt and PeopleWriteGuardTest.kt; the 25 test-case names are copied into the row's log.

clause (the spec's words): people_group_action:text → the SMS role holder's compose … resumes with smsto: both numbers (dumpsys activity activities; the intent's data holds both)
why it cannot hold as written: (1) The Fossify Messages fixture receives ACTION_SENDTO in a trampoline (NewConversationActivity) that forwards to its thread page and finishes, so `dumpsys activity activities` taken after the launch no longer holds the smsto: intent (E27 run 1, kept). (2) Android prints an smsto: URI redacted (every character an x) in dumpsys and in the system log alike, so "the data holds both" cannot be read as text from the system.
what the driver asserts instead: e27.sh asserts: the role holder is the resumed activity (dumpsys activity activities); the activity manager's own START line read from logcat since the tap — act=SENDTO, dat=smsto:, cmp the role holder's, from the shell's uid — whose redacted data is 25 characters (= "+15550000001;+15550000002"); the compose window's own dump naming Ann Lee and Bob Stone; and the shell's `[people] action text -> <holder> smsto:+15550000001;+15550000002` line.

clause (the spec's words): Text: "the SMS role holder's compose … resumes with smsto: her number (dumpsys activity activities)"
why it cannot hold as written: The same two facts as E27's: Fossify's trampoline (NewConversationActivity) has finished by the time of a dump, and Android redacts an smsto: URI.
what the driver asserts instead: e12.sh asserts the role holder resumed (dumpsys activity activities), the activity manager's START line from logcat since the tap (act=SENDTO, dat=smsto:, the holder's component, from the shell's uid, redacted data 12 characters = "+15550000001"), the compose window naming her, and the shell's `[people] action text -> <holder> smsto:+15550000001` line. Confirmed by the row's passing run on 3c1ad1e0 (`E12/`).

clause (the spec's words): Call: "`dumpsys telecom` shows an outgoing call placed by the shell and `adb emu gsm list` lists it (`gsm cancel` after)"
why it cannot hold as written: On this image `adb emu gsm list` prints only `OK`, with or without a call up (INDEX Change Log 2026-10-01; the builder's DEV-CALLPROBE), and the emulated network ends a call to the row's own number (+1 555 000 0001) about a quarter of a second after Telecom creates it (DisconnectCause REMOTE / NORMAL), so no dump can catch it up.
what the driver asserts instead: e12.sh RECORDs `adb emu gsm list` (after the call to her own number, and again while a call is up: "OK" both times) and asserts the call from Telecom's own record: one more `CallTC@n … (MO - outgoing)` entry than before the tap, whose event log holds `CREATED (app.tileshell; …)`. A second number the network keeps up (5551230001, added to Ann's card as a second phone row) is called too: while it is up Telecom's dump names it the foreground call (`[Call id=TC@n, state=ACTIVE …]`, no SET_DISCONNECTED in its record), then `adb emu gsm cancel` and END CALL, and Telecom's mCalls is asserted empty. Confirmed by the row's passing run on 3c1ad1e0 (`E12/`).

clause (the spec's words): `adb shell content read --uri <the uri from that line>` yields text beginning BEGIN:VCARD with FN:Ann Lee and her TEL
why it cannot hold as written: `content read` opens a plain file and the Contacts provider serves a vCard as an asset stream: on this image it answers "java.io.FileNotFoundException: No files supported by provider" (INDEX Change Log 2026-10-01; recorded in the row's log on every run).
what the driver asserts instead: e15.sh asserts the logged URI's form (content://com.android.contacts/contacts/as_vcard/<Ann's lookup>), `content query` on it (_display_name=Ann Lee.vcf) and `content gettype` (text/x-vcard), then hands the same URI to the image's Contacts app (VIEW text/x-vcard, read grant) and reads what it imported from the provider: name Ann Lee, a phone whose digits are 15550000001, e-mail ann@example.com. The imported raw contact is deleted by id. The literal first line "BEGIN:VCARD" is not read.

clause (the spec's words): Share: "`dumpsys activity activities` shows the resolver for ACTION_SEND text/x-vcard"
why it cannot hold as written: The resolver is Android's chooser, started with ACTION_CHOOSER; dumpsys prints its own intent (act=android.intent.action.CHOOSER, clip={text/uri-list …}, "has extras") and not the ACTION_SEND intent it wraps or that intent's type.
what the driver asserts instead: e15.sh asserts: the chooser (com.android.intentresolver) is the resumed activity with act=CHOOSER; its window previews "Ann Lee.vcf"; the one URI grant naming a vCard is for the logged URI, read-only, from the Contacts provider to the resolver; `content gettype` on the logged URI is text/x-vcard; the apps receiving ACTION_SEND text/x-vcard on the image are RECORDed.

clause (the spec's words): APK: `stat -c%s` before task 2 and after task 8 differ by ≤ 2 MB, `unzip -l` shows no new entry ≥ 1 MB
why it cannot hold as written: The lead's clause (QA brief): the merged debug APK is 3,405,518 bytes over the pre-task-2 one and two more dex files pass 1 MB, all code — put to the owner (INDEX Change Log 2026-10-01).
what the driver asserts instead: e15.sh asserts nothing about the APK and says so with a `record` line.

clause (the spec's words): fields 32 epx (34 with an edit button)
why it cannot hold as written: The 34-epx pencil variant on Name and Company is not built (INDEX Change Log 2026-10-01, P3: no structured-name sub-editor).
what the driver asserts instead: e20.sh asserts what is drawn: every field box measured on the pixels is 32 ± 1 epx with its 2-epx (133,133,133) border from x 12 to W − 12, and RECORDs that no edit button node is drawn beside the Name field.

clause (the spec's words): the CONTACTS / GROUPS pivot header in semibold caps
why it cannot hold as written: A font's weight is not a dump attribute.
what the driver asserts instead: e20.sh asserts the caps from the node text and the weight from the pixels: the header's stem thickness over its cap height is at least 1.2 × that of the regular-weight contact name on the same screen (measured: about 1.3–1.5 ×).

clause (the spec's words): a 60-fps screenrecord of the same 40 s corroborates under phase 05's frame-spacing rule (RV11; never the clock)
why it cannot hold as written: The row gives no criterion for "corroborates". The emulator's screenrecord is variable-rate (a frame only when the screen changed).
what the driver asserts instead: e11.sh records the same 40 s at 540 × 1170 and reads its motion bursts inside the PEOPLE tile's bounds — a frame moves when the region differs at all from the frame before (> 0.002 levels). Each logged slide is matched to the burst at its time; a burst whose source frames lie more than 18.2 ms apart is rejected (phase 05's rule); an accepted one must span the logged settle less one frame, ± 2 frames (phase 13 E8's band). Asserted: at least one out-slide and one in-slide corroborated, and no accepted capture contradicting the shell's clock; the counts are RECORDed. Also RECORDed for H3: at phase 13's 0.2-level threshold the in-slide reads about 370–385 ms — its ease-out spends the last third of the 583 ms inside the last capture pixel.

clause (the spec's words): a birthday on Ann whose month-day is the DEVICE's own today … "the Calendar app shows it on today's date, the tile shows it today … and Tess's typed 'what is on my calendar' names it"
why it cannot hold as written: An all-day event's instance is the UTC day [00:00, 24:00) of its date, and the tile's and Tess's reads are Instances over [now, now + 24 h] (CalendarFeed, ActionLayer.calendarToday). In a zone behind UTC a birthday on the LOCAL today therefore leaves the tile and Tess at 18:00 local (MDT) — the row would pass at 17:35 (it did, on build 686506a7) and fail an hour later on the same product. Whether the tile and Tess should keep showing today's all-day event until local midnight is a product question for the owner (phase 14's pod already reads from the start of today); the lead asked for a time-proof fixture.
what the driver asserts instead: e17.sh gives Ann the month-day of the device's current UTC date (the local today before 18:00 MDT, the local tomorrow after), so the event's all-day instance always holds "now". Every clause is asserted for that date: the Calendar app shows it on that date (its Day view's all-day band and the Agenda's heading), the tile shows it, the pod lists it, Tess names it. Bob's no-year birthday is the date after. Both dates are RECORDed against the device's local date.

clause (the spec's words): phase 03 E10's gated calendar commands are unchanged and re-run passing and "Phase 03 E7 (text / call by name) and E14 (person reminder) re-run passing on the same fixtures"
why it cannot hold as written: qa/phase-03/scripts/e10.sh, e7.sh and e14.sh SPEAK every request (speak.sh: the microphone, the host's or the emulator's injected audio), and no row of this phase uses the microphone (Acceptance preamble, V20; the QA rules). They cannot be re-run unchanged. (j6.sh types its request, so it IS re-run unchanged, twice, as the row says.)
what the driver asserts instead: e9.sh leg G: a PIN set and the keyguard up, Tess opened over it, the typed "what is on my calendar" and "add a meeting called standup to my calendar at ten AM" each show cortana_card:unlock reading "Unlock to continue", nothing is added, the keyguard stays; the PIN is cleared after. Leg N on provision.sh's Mom: the typed "text Mom running late" → cortana_card:text_readback naming Mom, "call Mom" → cortana_card:call_confirm naming Mom, both cancelled with nothing sent or dialled; the typed "remind me to ask about dinner next time I talk to Mom" → the person card with its contact chip, confirm → the saved card's subline, then an incoming text from Mom's number (adb emu sms send) fires the reminder. E14's other three firing paths and E7's and E10's remaining clauses are not re-proven here.

clause (the spec's words): Every "at x <n>" of a line of text or a glyph (the month title at x 51.0, day headings at x 24, the label at x 24.3, the title at x 92.5, week labels at x 10, account headers at x 14, calendar names at x 62), ± 1 epx
why it cannot hold as written: R11's positions are half-level crossings of the INK in its screenshots, while the product places each text's BOX at R11's x; a glyph's side bearing (0.3–1.5 epx at these sizes) then decides the result, and R11 does not say which glyph it measured for every value.
what the driver asserts instead: cal_geo.py measures the ink's left edge (half-level crossing, as R11 did) and e19.sh's fixtures use R11's own sample text where R11 names it: titles "Pay rent" / "Ride a bike" and a Saturday heading (C1 083), a week whose labels start with "2" ("23 MON", C2 311), calendar names "MoNa Events" / "mark guim" (WCS); each assertion's name says which text was measured, and the text box's own left edge is RECORDed beside it. Week labels that start with another digit are recorded, not asserted. Today's heading is asserted at the ink only on a Wednesday (R11's sample is "Wednesday 2"); on another weekday its text box's left edge is asserted and the ink recorded. "Semibold" is asserted as stroke weight: the commonest stem width over the cap height ≥ 0.16 (regular lines read 0.09–0.15 on the same screens). 1-epx and 2-epx lines are held to one device pixel (± 0.34 epx), tighter than the row's ± 1.

clause (the spec's words): the Agenda dump holds exactly ONE cal_event_title: node reading 'Standup' … (the Day and Week views the same), with the fixture "a local event 'Standup' starting 2 hours from the device's now, 1 hour long"
why it cannot hold as written: Run between 21:00 and 23:00 the fixture crosses midnight, and an event on two days is listed on each of them (the product's multi-day rule, E5): the Agenda and the Week view then hold two Standup nodes, both the LOCAL event's (kept run: E24-run1-standup-crossed-midnight, 21:39 MDT). Nothing of the copy shows.
what the driver asserts instead: e24.sh asserts one cal_event_title node reading Standup for EACH day the event covers that the view shows (one day at most hours, two when it crosses midnight), every one carrying the local id, plus no cal_event:<copy id> node in each view; the Day view of its start holds exactly one. The covered days are RECORDed.

clause (the spec's words): (e): "Android's Settings in front, pm clear app.tileshell (the shell is stopped, its store gone); jump_clock past A's T−10 min, so A's alert comes due while no shell runs"
why it cannot hold as written: On this AVD the system starts the shell again within 3 s of pm clear, Settings in front or not (it holds the HOME and ASSISTANT roles, the notification listener and the keyboard): run 1 on build 3c1ad1e0 read pid 2464 and a new calendar_sync.json with remindersSince BEFORE A's alarm time, so A was not older than the shell's first start and was (rightly) notified. The leg's precondition cannot hold after pm clear alone (kept run: E6-run1-leg-e-precondition-failed-pm-clear-restarts-the-shell).
what the driver asserts instead: e6.sh runs pm clear as written, RECORDs the pid 3 s later, and when the shell is running again it runs adb uninstall app.tileshell (the store goes with the package); it then asserts no shell process before AND after the jump and no store, A's alert row present (state 0 or 1), runs provision.sh (which installs the build under test — the first start is then after A came due), asserts remindersSince > A's alarm time, and from there the leg is as written.

clause (the spec's words): every clock move here is FORWARDS (jump_clock) together with (d) "adb reboot with a reminder 3 min ahead"
why it cannot hold as written: Legs (a) and (b) leave the device clock about 40 minutes ahead of the host's; the emulator's clock after a reboot is the host's (the row RECORDs device and host equal right after boot), so a reminder set 3 minutes ahead of a jumped clock would not be 3 minutes ahead after the reboot.
what the driver asserts instead: Before leg (d) e6.sh saves the ring and runs clock_restore (its force-stop and Home are the preamble's form for a backwards step), sets the 3-minute reminder on the restored clock, reboots, and takes leg (d)'s MARK after the boot; legs (a)–(c) and (e) only ever jump forwards.

clause (the spec's words): People with 5,000 contacts (a driver loop; the list's dump of the top rows is available within 3 s, the jump grid still lands on its letter)
why it cannot hold as written: (1) A `content insert` loop of 10,000 device-shell calls (a raw contact and its name each) would hold the shared emulator for the better part of an hour. (2) A uiautomator dump has no time stamp of its own and takes one to two seconds by itself.
what the driver asserts instead: edge_P01 makes the 5,000 the way a user gets that many — one vCard file imported by the image's own Contacts app into the phone's account (19 s on the kept run; counted from the provider: 5000) — and removes them by their name pattern in one sync-adapter delete. "Within 3 s" is asserted on the shell's own line: `[people] list: 5002 contacts …` is written within 3000 ms of a MARK taken before `am start -W` (175 ms on the kept run), `am start -W` reports the launch complete, and the dump taken straight after holds people_row: nodes; the dump's own completion time is not stamped. The jump is asserted as written (the M header and an M name on screen after people_jump_cell:M).

clause (the spec's words): Mail: "with the slot unassigned → Android's resolver"
why it cannot hold as written: Android shows its resolver only when two or more activities can take the intent. On this image ONE activity handles ACTION_SENDTO mailto: (eu.faircode.email/.ActivityCompose; K-9 with no account resolves none), so Android starts it with no page of its own.
what the driver asserts instead: e12.sh RECORDs the image's mailto: handlers and asserts: the shell names no component (`[people] action mail -> resolver mailto:ann@example.com`); with one handler the resumed activity is that handler and its intent is `act=android.intent.action.SENDTO dat=mailto:ann@example.com` (dumpsys activity activities); with two or more it would assert the resolver resumed. The resolver's own page for a contact intent IS driven in the row's VIEW leg.

clause (the spec's words): Address: "OsmAnd resumes with a geo: query" (read from dumpsys activity activities, as the row's other launches are)
why it cannot hold as written: OsmAnd takes VIEW geo: in a trampoline (GeoIntentActivity) that hands on to its map page and finishes, so a dump seconds later holds only the map page's own intent; and Android prints a geo: URI redacted ("dat=geo:").
what the driver asserts instead: e12.sh asserts OsmAnd resumed (dumpsys activity activities), the activity manager's START line from logcat since the tap (act=VIEW, dat=geo:, cmp=net.osmand.plus/…, from the shell's uid), and the query's text from the shell's own line: `[people] action map -> net.osmand.plus/.activities.MapActivity geo:0,0?q=1%20Main%20St%20Springfield`. The emulator stayed up through the map action on both runs (2026-10-01 23:53 and 2026-10-02 00:19).

clause (the spec's words): the typed 'what is on my calendar' (no apostrophe, V20) names the events inserted for the test, after "add a calendar event called dentist tomorrow at 2 pm"
why it cannot hold as written: Tess's read covers the next 24 hours (ActionLayer.calendarToday: Instances over now … now + 24 h). "Tomorrow at 2 pm" is inside them only when the row runs after 14:00; run at 00:26 the dentist is 37 h away and is rightly not named (kept run: E9-run2-dentist-outside-tess-24-hours-at-0026, its one failure).
what the driver asserts instead: e9.sh inserts its own event "E9 checkup" one hour ahead and asserts Tess names it at any hour; it asserts "dentist" is named when its start is inside 24 hours of the request and NOT named (with the hours RECORDed) when it is outside.

clause (the spec's words): the tile's face is the day only (phase 01's existing behaviour)
why it cannot hold as written: A live tile shows its feed's face in turn with its own front (the icon and the name): over 8 dumps a second apart the CALENDAR tile reads "Friday | 2 | Calendar" in some and "Calendar" alone in the others, so "the day only" cannot be read as "every dump shows the day".
what the driver asserts instead: edge_C01 asserts that the dumps hold exactly one distinct text with the day in it (the day name and number), that every other dump reads the tile's name alone (no event text in any), and RECORDs the feed's refresh line.

clause (the spec's words): a Sync tapped twice quickly (one copy; the second compares the copy with the local event and writes nothing, `ok`)
why it cannot hold as written: Quickly has no number, and adb cannot tap twice in one instant: two `input tap` processes started together interleave their DOWN and UP and the app receives ONE click (the kept grouped run EDGE-cal-run1-C01-to-C17-220-7-14: one sync line).
what the driver asserts instead: edge_C05 starts the second tap's process 0.2 s after the first's. Kept run EDGE-cal-run3-C05-alone-41-0-2: the two sync lines are 196 ms apart (`updated`, then `ok`), one copy carrying the pushed title; on a first Sync (the picker's target tapped twice the same way) one line and one copy.

clause (the spec's words): rows changing under the observer (a `content insert` loop of 50 events over 10 s)
why it cannot hold as written: Each `content insert` starts a process on the device; 50 of them as two workers side by side took 23 s on this AVD, not 10 (RECORDed). A loop held to 10 s would need more workers, which changes the load, not the clause's point.
what the driver asserts instead: edge_C10 runs the 50 inserts under the open Day view in the time they take (RECORDed) and asserts what the clause is about: the view's last `view day` line counts the 50 more, the view shows them, the same process, no new crash entry.

clause (the spec's words): a locale change re-labels months and the first day of the week without a restart
why it cannot hold as written: The clause does not say which locale. The sub-step does not change the SYSTEM locale of the shared emulator (every other row and both writers read its English texts); it changes the shell's own app locale (`cmd locale set-app-locales app.tileshell --locales de-DE`), which reaches the app as a configuration change. A system-locale change was not driven.
what the driver asserts instead: edge_C15 sets the shell's app locale to de-DE and back: the header reads the month in German ("OKTOBER 2026"), the strip's first day goes from Sunday to Monday, the shell's pid is unchanged; restored to no app locale and asserted.
